description: Prepare the project for its future shape: (a) organise/name modules so secondary and primary schools are clearly separated from the start (only secondary exists now; primary comes later and must not force a rename/restructure), and (b) plan + wire the PyPI package: a public install-and-call API that takes data + a report type and returns HTML or PDF, with all needed fonts packaged (including the legally-awkward ones, for now, so installers see the real expected output), no fallback fonts ever, and total package size kept well under 100MB. The user asked for the restructuring to be done so future primary work is painless, and for a concrete packaging PLAN plus the working API shape. Keep the fidelity guardrail intact throughout - any code move must not change rendered output.
steps: Design the secondary/primary separation and write it up in docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md: identify what is secondary-school-specific today (report families, schemas, layout specs, extractors, competency bands) versus what is generic mechanism (layout, layout_spec, fonts, printing, binding, template_maker). Propose a namespacing where secondary lives under a clearly-secondary path (e.g. src/sars/secondary/ or a `level`-scoped package) and generic mechanism stays shared, so a future src/sars/primary/ slots in without renaming existing modules. Decide how far to physically move code now: at minimum, introduce the secondary namespace for the report-family-specific pieces and re-export from the current locations so nothing breaks, keeping the move small and pixel-neutral. Record any moves as a mechanical, output-preserving refactor.

If code is moved, prove it is inert: re-run `python -m sars.cli data && python -m sars.cli template && python tools/compare.py && python tools/fidelity_gate.py --json output/fidelity/current.json` and confirm no report's worst-page-visible dropped versus baseline, and `pytest -q -m "not slow"` still passes. If a full physical move is too risky to keep pixel-neutral in one feature, deliver the concrete documented plan + the namespace scaffolding + re-exports, and record the remaining moves as follow-ups in docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md.

Define and implement the public package API (the whole point of packaging): a stable, documented entry point where a caller installs the package, supplies data (a schema instance or its JSON/dict) and a report type, and gets back HTML or PDF bytes/path. Build on the existing sars.template_maker (render_html/render_pdf/make) and schema.from_dict; expose a clean top-level import (e.g. `from sars import render_html, render_pdf` or a documented `sars.api`) that also accepts plain dict/JSON data via schema.from_dict, and list the valid report types (templates.TEMPLATE_NAMES / schema.SCHEMA_BY_TYPE). Add a short usage example to README.md and docs.

Write docs/PACKAGING.md: the concrete PyPI plan. Cover (1) how fonts are packaged: today assets/fonts is a gitignored build artefact derived from sars.zip by tools/build_fonts.py - the package must ship the fonts it needs so an installer gets the real expected output. Specify the packaging mechanism (include the derived font files as package data, or ship them zipped / as a post-install/first-run build step from the bundled sars.zip, or as a separate downloadable font dependency the user fetches at install/first-use). For the legally-problematic faces (Monotype Arial etc.), the requirement is: include them anyway FOR NOW (as a zip / forced inclusion / user-downloaded dependency) so anyone installing can see the actual output, documented as removable later. NEVER use fallback fonts. (2) package size budget: measure current asset sizes (sars.zip ~9.1MB, layouts ~1.7MB, built fonts vary) and show the total stays well under 100MB; if bundling raw fonts + sars.zip approaches the budget, choose the smallest sufficient mechanism (e.g. ship sars.zip and build fonts on first run rather than shipping both). (3) build backend / package-data wiring in pyproject.toml (currently setuptools with packages.find where=src; templates/layouts/*.json.gz must be included as package data, and whatever font mechanism is chosen). (4) the console entry point (sars = sars.cli:main) and the library API from step 3.

Wire the minimum packaging that can be verified now WITHOUT publishing: ensure src/sars/templates/layouts/*.json.gz (and any chosen font/data assets) are declared as package data so `python -m build` (or `uv build`) produces an sdist+wheel that, when inspected, contains the layout specs and the API is importable. Do NOT push or publish. Confirm the built artifact size is well under 100MB.

Add fast tests: (a) the public API renders HTML and PDF from a dict/JSON round-tripped through schema.from_dict for at least one report type; (b) an import test that the documented top-level API symbols exist; (c) a package-data test that the layout specs resolve when loaded via importlib.resources / the packaged path. `pytest -q -m "not slow"` passes.
acceptance_criteria: docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md defines the secondary/primary separation and the namespace where future primary work slots in without renaming existing modules; any code moved is proven pixel-neutral (gate shows no report below baseline) or the remaining moves are documented as follow-ups with scaffolding + re-exports in place.

A documented public API lets a caller supply data (schema instance OR dict/JSON) + a report type and get back HTML string or PDF bytes/path, building on template_maker + schema.from_dict, with valid report types listed.

docs/PACKAGING.md gives a concrete PyPI plan covering the font-bundling mechanism (including the legally-awkward fonts, included for now, no fallback fonts), a measured package-size budget kept well under 100MB, pyproject package-data wiring, and the entry points.

`uv build` (or `python -m build`) produces an sdist + wheel that include the layout specs as package data and expose the importable API; the built artifact is well under 100MB. Nothing is published or pushed.
Fast tests cover the public API render-from-dict, the top-level API imports, and package-data resolution; `pytest -q -m "not slow"` passes.
The fidelity gate still shows no report below its baseline worst-page-visible.
verification: `. .venv/bin/activate && pytest -q -m "not slow"` -> exit 0 including the new API/packaging tests.
`uv build` (or `python -m build`) -> produces dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz; inspecting the wheel shows templates/layouts/*.json.gz present and total size well under 100MB.
`python tools/fidelity_gate.py --json output/fidelity/current.json` -> no report below its baseline worst-page-visible after any code moves.
